A melanoma section. Forty channels, about two hundred thousand cells.
To gate it, open Plexora AI, choose auto-thresholding, and say what the tissue is.
Plexora runs the statistics itself. The AI looks at the cells, and judges whether each gate makes sense.
C D forty-five first. Plexora proposes a gate, and the AI checks cells below it, at it, and above it.
Clean membrane rings, and SOX ten dark in every one. The gate holds.
SOX ten is easy. Two clean populations, so the gate stays as it is.
C D three is harder. Cells just under the gate look positive, so it compares lower thresholds, side by side.
It settles on one, but notes some signal spilling in from neighbours. Accepted, with low confidence.
E-cadherin and Ki sixty-seven were missing real positives too. Both come down.
For C D eight and C D sixty-eight, no threshold separates stained cells from unstained ones. Those, it leaves for you.
And C D twenty. The stain worked, but nothing here is truly positive, so it won't invent a population.
Eight markers in about three minutes, each written back with its confidence, and a note on why.
